stem: What is the primary difference between sensitization and a clinical food allergy?

options.text: Sensitization refers to a positive test result without symptoms, while clinical allergy requires symptoms upon exposure.
Sensitization is a delayed reaction, while clinical allergy is always immediate.
Sensitization only occurs in adults, whereas clinical allergies are found in children.
Sensitization refers to low antibody levels, while clinical allergy refers to high antibody levels.

explanation: Diagnosis of a true allergy requires both the presence of specific antibodies and a physical reaction when the food is ingested.
rationale: One is an immunological observation, the other is a symptomatic diagnosis.

optionExplanations.A: Diagnosis of a true allergy requires both the presence of specific antibodies and a physical reaction when the food is ingested.
optionExplanations.B: Sensitization is an immunological state of readiness, not a description of the timing of a reaction.
optionExplanations.C: Both sensitization and clinical allergy can be present across all age groups, though rates vary.
optionExplanations.D: While high levels increase the likelihood of allergy, the defining factor is the presence or absence of clinical symptoms.
